label: copy-phase input p late in the copy, strongest when the next output is 0 ("p0" bigram)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and almost always (98% of activation mass) on steps where the fed-back input is the letter p. The rest is on input 0 right after a p. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases. Magnitude goes up with position: the rate climbs steeply with t and recall_idx (about 0 for recall_idx<=2, highest at t=16-17), so long sequences (L=8-9) dominate. It is strongest when the token being output after the p is 0, i.e. the original contained the bigram p 0. The top examples are all p followed by 0, and p-input with out_tok 0 covers 65% of mass. A copy-phase p followed by a letter fires only weakly, and only late in the sequence. It does not fire on p at early copy positions, even before a 0. Precision is incomplete: copy-phase p is 30x enriched but only about 3.5% of those steps fire. p->0 with t>=10 gives dev precision 0.74, recall 0.40, mass 0.61. Dropping the 0 condition raises mass recall to about 0.87 but precision falls to about 0.07. No history variable explained which of the remaining p steps fire.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=p (+6.74), phase=2 & in_tok=0 (+5.59), in_tok=p (+4.19), next_out=0 (+3.76), phase=2 & out_tok=0 (+3.56), out_tok=0 (+3.40). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.05), prev_tok=<DEL> (-3.30), recall_idx=1 (-3.30), out_tok=v (-2.69).
